title: Simple Harmonic Motion: A Special Periodic Motion
lead: The oscillations of a system whose net force obeys Hooke’s law are the simplest and the most common. This section names them simple harmonic motion, shows that their period depends on the mass and the force constant alone, and follows the position, velocity and acceleration through one cycle to find the sine waves that connect oscillations to waves.
objectives: Explain the link between simple harmonic motion and waves.
summary_html:
• Simple harmonic motion is oscillatory motion for a system that can be described only by Hooke’s law. Such a system is also called a simple harmonic oscillator.
  • Maximum displacement is the amplitude $\kX$. The period $\kT$ and frequency $\kf$ of a simple harmonic oscillator are given by $\kT = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{\kk}}$ and $\kf = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{\kk}{m}}$, where $m$ is the mass of the system.
  • Displacement in simple harmonic motion as a function of time is given by $\kx(\kt) = \kX\cos\frac{2\pi\kt}{\kT}.$
  • The velocity is given by $\kv(\kt) = -\kvmax\sin\frac{2\pi\kt}{\kT}$, where $\kvmax = \kX\sqrt{\frac{\kk}{m}}$.
  • The acceleration is found to be $\ka(\kt) = -\frac{\kk\kX}{m}\cos\frac{2\pi\kt}{\kT}.$
